# IEC 60601-1 — Medical electrical equipment — Part 1: General requirements for basic safety and essential performance

_Demo sample data — not for clinical use._

**Standard**: IEC 60601-1:2005 + A1:2012 (Edition 3.1) is the designation cited by the PP3500 DHF (DI-010). The current FDA-recognized versions are **Edition 3.2** (IEC 60601-1:2005+A1:2012+A2:2020, consolidated 2020-08, FDA recognition **19-49**) and **ANSI/AAMI ES60601-1** (consolidated text incl. AMD2:2021, FDA recognition **19-46**) — see the edition question below. Publisher page for Ed 3.2: <https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/67497>.
**Category**: Medical electrical equipment — basic safety and essential performance
**Referenced In**: FDA Recognized Consensus Standards database — recognition 19-49 (IEC 60601-1 Edition 3.2 2020-08 consolidated version, Complete, recognized with relevant US national differences applied; entered 04/03/2023) and recognition 19-46 (ANSI/AAMI ES60601-1:2005/(R)2012 & A1:2012, C1:2009/(R)2012 & A2:2010/(R)2012 (Cons. Text) [Incl. AMD2:2021], Complete; entered 05/30/2022). Database search (2026-07-15): <https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfStandards/results.cfm?start_search=1&sortcolumn=std&referencenumber=60601-1>; 19-49 detail: <https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfStandards/detail.cfm?standard__identification_no=44029>. Cited in the 510(k) declaration-of-conformity strategy for the PP3500 hardware.
**Module Applicability**: Custom medical electrical hardware of the infusion pump — power supply, motor drive, fluid delivery assembly, user-facing electrical interfaces, and any associated accessories

## Overview

IEC 60601-1 establishes general requirements for basic safety and essential performance of medical electrical (ME) equipment and ME systems; for particular equipment types these requirements are supplemented or modified by collateral (60601-1-x) and particular (60601-2-x) standards (publisher abstract, <https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/67497>). It applies to this project because the infusion device includes custom medical electrical hardware — notably the mains/battery power subsystem, motor drive for the pump mechanism, fluid delivery assembly, and user-facing electrical interfaces (display, controls, alarms). Software aspects integrate with IEC 62304; risk management integrates with ISO 14971; usability with IEC 62366-1.

The Edition 3.2 consolidated version incorporates corrigenda 1 (2006), 2 (2007), and 3 (2022), the corrigendum to Amendment 1 (2014), and interpretation sheets 1 (2008), 2 (2009), 3 (2013) plus the interpretation sheet to Amendment 1 (2021) (<https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/67497>). ## PP3500 Applicability

_How the PainEase PCA Advanced (PP3500) DHF cites this standard. Demo sample data — not for clinical use._

**Design inputs that cite it:**

- **DI-010 (SAFE, CTS)** — the primary citation: the device shall meet the general electrical-safety and essential-performance requirements of "IEC 60601-1 (3rd edition + A1)" and the particular standard IEC 60601-2-24. Acceptance: third-party safety testing report, all applicable clauses, no deviations. (`docs/project/dhfs/pca-device/design-controls/requirements/design-inputs.md`, group G4)
- **DI-012 (INTE, CTS)** — EMC per collateral IEC 60601-1-2 (4th edition) for professional healthcare facility environments; third-party EMC test report.
- **DI-019 (INTE, CTF)** — audible alarms per collateral IEC 60601-1-8 (high/medium/low priority, SPL 45–80 dB(A) at 1 m); acoustic measurement in anechoic chamber.
- Related: **DI-006** cites the particular standard IEC 60601-2-24 §201.12.1.103 for free-flow protection bench testing. [VERIFY — clause number against the purchased IEC 60601-2-24]

**Hazards controlled by it** (`docs/project/dhfs/pca-device/risk-management/GL-TMP-RM-003-hazard-analysis.md`):

- **HAZ-008** — Alarm failure (not annunciated / not heard): DI-019 (60601-1-8 alarm scheme) + DI-010 (60601-1 / 60601-2-24 essential-performance compliance covering alarm-function integrity).
- **HAZ-009** — Electrical shock: DI-010 electrical-safety design per IEC 60601-1 (3rd edition + A1) and IEC 60601-2-24 — insulation, leakage-current limits, applied-part isolation. Post-control S4/P1 Acceptable.
- **HAZ-016** — Mechanical failure (drop / mount detachment): DI-010 enclosure and mechanical robustness per IEC 60601-1, plus DI-033 mass/mounting.
- Related: **HAZ-010** (EMC disturbance) is controlled via DI-012 / collateral IEC 60601-1-2, not the general standard directly.

**Verification method:** third-party (accredited-lab) safety test report against all applicable IEC 60601-1 / IEC 60601-2-24 clauses with no deviations (per DI-010 acceptance criteria and the HAZ-008/009/016 verification columns). EMC and acoustic-alarm evidence are separate third-party/bench reports under DI-012 / DI-019.

**Edition question (open):** the DHF (DI-010, HAZ-009) cites **"3rd edition + A1"** = Edition 3.1 (IEC 60601-1:2005+A1:2012). The current FDA recognitions are **Edition 3.2** (2005+A1:2012+A2:2020, recognition 19-49, with US national differences) and **AAMI ES60601-1 incl. AMD2:2021** (recognition 19-46). Before test-lab engagement and the 510(k) declaration of conformity, the program must either (a) update DI-010 to the FDA-recognized designation it will declare against, or (b) justify the Ed 3.1 citation via the transition provisions of the recognition entry. [VERIFY — resolve with regulatory affairs; check the extent-of-recognition and transition notes on the 19-49 detail page, <https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfStandards/detail.cfm?standard__identification_no=44029>]

**Particular-standard recognition gap:** a designation search for **IEC 60601-2-24** (infusion pumps and controllers) in the FDA Recognized Consensus Standards database on 2026-07-15 returned **no records** (<https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfStandards/results.cfm?start_search=1&sortcolumn=std&referencenumber=60601-2-24>), while AAMI TIR101:2021 (fluid delivery performance testing for infusion pumps) IS recognized (6-482, Complete). [VERIFY — 60601-2-24 recognition status and how FDA infusion-pump guidance expects conformity to be shown; DI-006/DI-010 cite it as if recognized.]

## Key Requirements

The clause numbers below follow the 3rd-edition structure per the registry distillation's clause-topic map — [VERIFY] against the purchased standard before citing any clause in a deliverable; normative wording, test methods, and limit values live only in the standard itself.

### Clause 4 — General requirements

[VERIFY] Risk management process (links to ISO 14971), essential-performance identification, expected service life, and single fault conditions.

### Clause 5 — General requirements for testing of ME equipment

[VERIFY] Type tests, sequence of tests, environmental conditions.

### Clause 6 — Classification of ME equipment and ME systems

[VERIFY] Protection against electric shock (Class I/II, Type B/BF/CF applied parts), ingress protection, mode of operation.

### Clause 7 — ME equipment identification, marking, and documents

[VERIFY] Marking on the outside of equipment, accompanying documents, instructions for use.

### Clause 8 — Protection against electrical hazards

[VERIFY] Means of protection (MOOP/MOPP), leakage currents, dielectric strength, insulation, creepage and clearance distances. Cited (by topic) as the risk control for HAZ-009 electrical shock.

### Clause 9 — Protection against mechanical hazards

[VERIFY] Moving parts (motor drive, pump mechanism), stability, expelled parts, surfaces, corners, edges. Cited (by topic) as the risk control for HAZ-016 mechanical failure.

### Clause 10 — Protection against unwanted and excessive radiation hazards

[VERIFY] Applicability to infusion device under review.

### Clause 11 — Protection against excessive temperatures and other hazards

[VERIFY] Temperature of applied parts, fire, overflow, spillage, cleaning and disinfection compatibility, biocompatibility coordination with ISO 10993.

### Clause 12 — Accuracy of controls and instruments and protection against hazardous outputs

[VERIFY] Accuracy of delivery (dose/rate) — coordinate with IEC 60601-2-24 particular standard for infusion pumps.

### Clause 13 — Hazardous situations and fault conditions

[VERIFY] Single fault conditions and their evaluation.

### Clause 14 — Programmable electrical medical systems (PEMS)

[VERIFY] Interface to IEC 62304 software lifecycle for PEMS development process.

### Clause 15 — Construction of ME equipment

[VERIFY] Mechanical construction, containers, connectors, mains parts. With Clause 9, the topical home of the HAZ-016 enclosure-robustness control.

### Clause 16 — ME systems

[VERIFY] System-level requirements when ME equipment is combined with other equipment (e.g., EHR connection pathway).

### Clause 17 — Electromagnetic compatibility

[VERIFY] Reference to collateral IEC 60601-1-2 for EMC.
